# Unit 4 Week 9 student workbook
Two explicit lessons, plus two separate database workshops. Original practice draft.
Lesson 1 (approximately 50–55 minutes): 5 minutes distinguish ethics/law/policy; 10 minutes map five APPs and entity assumptions; 20 minutes pairs analyse P1–P6; 10 minutes compare P6/P7 and dates; 5–10 minutes explain feedback and fresh exit case. Explain APP 11 retention conditions, APP 12 access exceptions and why 30 days is not a blanket notification delay.
Lesson 2 (approximately 50–55 minutes): 10 minutes purpose/quality/data-mining critique of the fictional CSV; 5 minutes predict Python counts (teacher demonstration or manual counting); 15 minutes P8 paper red/blue scope/report; 15 minutes privacy and source decisions for the database project; 5–10 minutes peer review/exit. Do not add these tasks on top of the two project workshops.
Data task: count bookings by workshop, distinguish bookings from unique people, predict threshold-3 display, and explain identification risk from codes/rare combinations and outside knowledge. Compare an aggregate scheduling decision with an individual penalty. Missing data and correlation cannot establish motivation. The arbitrary suppression rule is not a release approval or anonymisation standard.
Project decisions: purpose/necessary fields; collection explanation; approved recipients/access; source date/accuracy; access requests; retention/backup obligations; testing evidence; ownership/control; accountable reviewer. Use fictional data and label proposed features separately from implemented features.
Exit: one principle applied to a fresh fact, one missing fact, one justified next step. No real-system testing, notices, uploads or personal records.
